haiku-low.q1: Pager fires after /healthz fails 3 times at 2 of 3 sites; a human runs failover --to B. Detection alone never fails over.
haiku-low.q2: The lag check halts the failover and unlocks if the replica's recorded lag exceeds 30 s. Then a human must override with accept-data-loss or abort.
haiku-low.q3: Promotion needs the lease, flag flipped to B and a passing lag check. Workers need requeue done. DNS needs DR green.
haiku-low.q4: Redis is per region and not replicated, so users sign in again on the standby. This is accepted.
haiku-low.q5: It is snapshotted for inspection, then wiped and rebuilt as a DR replica from a base backup. Returning to A is a separate planned switchover.
haiku-low.q6: Apps and workers in A need a good witness read naming A within 15 s to write, so partitioned A turns read-only within 20 s.
haiku-low.q7: The witness, a 3-node strongly consistent KV cluster across A, B and C. Only the runbook tool writes it; every app box and worker in A and B reads it every 5 s.
haiku-low.q8: Step 5 requeues jobs marked running; DR workers rerun them. Idempotent, job-id-keyed jobs are required since recent finished ones rerun too.
haiku-low.q9: Rerun failover --to B; it takes the lease and resumes at the first step lacking a done line. Going back to A via abort works only before promote's started line.
haiku-low.q10: It still lands on A until DNS cache expires, up to 60 s after GTM cutover. If A is up it gets stale reads and 503 writes; if A is down, requests fail.
haiku-low.q11: Up to the replica's recorded lag, max 30 s unless overridden; partitioned A's commits after the stream broke, up to 20 s after step 2, are also lost.

sonnet.q1: A human runs the failover tool (failover --to B) after the pager fires. Monitoring (3 probe sites, GET /healthz every 10 s) pages on-call when 3 consecutive fails occur at 2 of 3 sites; it never fails over by itself.
sonnet.q2: If the replica's recorded lag (as of the last WAL received from the primary) is over 30 s, the tool halts and gives up the lease, keeping its place in the log. It proceeds only if rerun with the accept-data-loss override, or the team aborts (failover --abort). Nobody can write during this time.
sonnet.q3: Before promotion: lease taken, flag flipped to B, write grants pulled on old primary (best effort), 20 s fence sleep done, and lag check passed (or overridden). Before B's workers start: promotion done and jobs requeued (step 5). Before DNS cutover: DR site scaled and green (standby LB and probes both pass /healthz, polled up to 5 min).
sonnet.q4: The session is lost: Redis is per region and not replicated, so everyone has to log in again on the standby. This is accepted.
sonnet.q5: There is no auto failback. When it comes back, its Postgres is snapshotted (to examine lost writes), then wiped and rebuilt as a replica of the DR site from a base backup. Returning to A is a separate planned switchover later. Meanwhile A's app tier stays read-only because the flag says B.
sonnet.q6: The witness-based fence. Every app box and worker polls the flag every 5 s and may start a DB write only if it had a good read in the last 15 s naming its own region (write transactions capped at 5 s). A cut-off region can't read the witness (needs 2 of 3), so it goes read-only; it is done committing 20 s after the flag names the other region or after it loses the witness. Pulling write grants is only best effort.
sonnet.q7: The witness, a 3-node strongly consistent KV cluster (one node each in A, B and Region C; reads and writes need 2 of 3), holds the active_region flag. Only the runbook tool (including its abort) writes it. Every app box and worker in both A and B polls it every 5 s. The witness also holds failover_log and the lease.
sonnet.q8: Step 5 (requeue) runs in the promoted DB before any DR worker exists. Jobs marked running are set back to queued and DR workers rerun them after step 6 starts them. Jobs A finished in its last unreplicated seconds also rerun. This requires jobs to be idempotent (keyed by job id).
sonnet.q9: If the tool dies, the lease expires within 30 s. Rerun failover --to B, which takes the lease and resumes at the first step without a done line, redoing a half-done step (all steps are safe to repeat). Going back to A is possible with failover --abort only before the promote has a started line. Abort takes the lease, sets the flag back to A, restores write grants on A's DB if step 2 pulled them, and closes the log. Once promote has started, abort is refused, even if the tool died mid-promotion. After that it is forward only.
sonnet.q10: From step 2 until their cached DNS expires (up to the 60 s TTL after GTM cutover) they still land on A. If A is up, they get reads from its stale DB and a 503 'read-only, retry shortly' on writes. If A is down, requests just fail. After the cache expires they reach B.
sonnet.q11: Whatever A committed that the replica never received (async WAL streaming). If A died, at most the replica's recorded lag, max 30 s unless the override was used. If A was partitioned and kept going, its commits after the stream was lost until it stopped writing (at the latest 20 s after step 2) are also lost. The lag check can't see these; they exist only in the old primary's snapshot.
